newsitem.title: USA: US concerned by Canada wheat exports - USTR official.
newsitem.headline: US concerned by Canada wheat exports - USTR official.

text.p: U.S. officials expressed "continuing concern" about high levels of Canadian wheat shipments to the U.S. market at a meeting last week, an official of the trade representative's office said Tuesday.

Marilyn Moore, a senior economist at USTR, said it was inaccurate to suggest, as one Canadian spokesman did after Friday's meeting in Ottawa, that the United States had agreed not to limit imports of Canadian grains.
For the past couple of years, the U.S. has monitored Canadian shipments with an eye to consultations if volume became excessive.

Canadian and U.S. officials have projected wheat and barley shipments to U.S. buyers would be about 1.4-1.5 million tonnes in the year ending September 12. That volume would be at the cap set in a 1994 agreement that has lapsed but still is regarded as a reference point for U.S. action.

Moore said the U.S.-Canada talks focused on factors behind the trade volume and ways to achieve greater understanding among farmers and processors of the policies used by each government and marketing methods in each country.
The nations will hold semiannual meetings on agricultural issues, Moore told the Millers National Federation meeting.
